hook: A chemist looking at a new formula wants to know, before doing anything else, which atoms are joined, by how many shared pairs, and where the spare electrons sit. A Lewis diagram answers all three in a sketch you can draw in a minute, as long as you count carefully.

prereq.q: How many valence electrons does a sulfur atom (group 16) have?
prereq.why: For groups 13-18, the number of valence electrons is the group number minus 10: S has 6 (3s² 3p⁴).

prereq.q: A double bond between two atoms is
options: one shared pair and one lone pair
two atoms each with an octet
prereq.why: Each shared pair is two electrons; a double bond shares two pairs.

figure.caption: Lewis diagrams of H₂O, NH₃, CO₂ and NH₄⁺. Each line is a bonding pair; each pair of dots is a lone pair. The ammonium ion is drawn in brackets with its charge.

chain.cause: Only valence electrons take part in bonding
chain.effect: a Lewis diagram shows only valence electrons, counted from each atom's group and the ion's charge

chain.cause: Bonding pairs are shared by two atoms
chain.effect: each line counts as two electrons for both atoms it joins

chain.cause: Eight valence electrons fill the valence s and p subshells
chain.effect: most period 2 atoms end with an octet; H ends with two

chain.cause: The central atom may be short of eight after outer atoms are complete
chain.effect: outer lone pairs become double or triple bonds

chain.cause: B has only three valence electrons, odd totals leave one unpaired, and period 3 atoms can hold more than eight
chain.effect: incomplete octets, free radicals and expanded octets are the exceptions

ideas: A Lewis diagram shows every valence electron: lines for bonding pairs, dot pairs for lone pairs.
Count first: group valence electrons for every atom, plus one per negative charge, minus one per positive charge.
Octet rule: most period 2 atoms end with eight electrons; H with two.
Put the central atom in the middle (never H), complete the outer atoms, put leftovers on the center, then make multiple bonds if the center is short.
Exceptions: incomplete octet (B), odd-electron species (NO), expanded octet from period 3 on (SF₆).

misconception.wrong: For a positive ion such as NH₄⁺, add an electron for the charge.
misconception.right: A positive charge means the species has lost electrons, so subtract one per + charge: NH₄⁺ has 5 + 4 − 1 = 8 electrons. Add electrons only for negative charges.

summary: A Lewis diagram shows a molecule's or ion's valence electrons as bonding pairs (lines) and lone pairs (dots). Count the valence electrons, adjusting for charge; connect the outer atoms to the central atom; complete the outer octets; put leftovers on the center; and form double or triple bonds if the center is short. Most period 2 atoms follow the octet rule and H has two electrons, but boron can have an incomplete octet, odd-electron species leave one electron unpaired, and atoms from period 3 on can have expanded octets.
